title: Legends Untold - The Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mM4k2pf-l9E

Daniel (@dungeondive) reviews Legends Untold from Inspiring Games, a 2019 Kickstarter he owns as two novice sets, The Great Sewers and The Weeping Caves, combined into a single box. Like Dark Venture, which he'd just reviewed, it packs a big experience into a small box. The mechanisms aren't complex, but there's a lot to remember from phase to phase.

The heroes are ordinary folk, not champions. His guttersnipe and follower recall Dungeon Crawl Classics, and the character cards echo FFG's third-edition Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay. Skills double as health: damage drains them, and with none left you fall unconscious. Each weapon carries its own 3d6 results table, so an attack can do far more than hit or miss. Roll under seven with a bow and the arrow lands in your own melee fighter. Scouting rolls against the light level leave the party alert, bold or careless, a scout and a guard handle positioning abstractly, and the event deck doubles as the timer.

He calls it "Legends Untold: Stat Check the Game" and means it as praise, and he recommends the designers' flowchart player aid. He'd like more traps and more time events. He also worries that the next set's promised "more story" will mean paragraphs to read rather than the emergent storytelling it already has.

----

Daniel hopes "more story" won't mean more paragraphs to read. Where do you draw the line between emergent narrative and text read off a card?
